newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Interest in Australian bonds dampened by holiday.
newsitem.headline: Interest in Australian bonds dampened by holiday.

text.p: *Australian bonds end markedly lower, but at day's highs, after being held to narrow ranges in holiday-affected trade.
*Focus to remain on U.S. market until Thursday's local labour force report for July.
A holiday-affected Australian bond market traded narrow ranges at markedly lower levels on Monday, after a sharp sell-off in the U.S. Treasury market on Friday.
Bonds opened near their weekend lows and held a soft tone until signs of weakness in the ANZ Bank job ads series for July saw them nudge higher. They ended the day at their highs.
With a bank holiday in New South Wales closing the Sydney Futures Exchange, trading was restricited to the SYCOM system normally used for after hours trading and volume was very light.
The week's key release is Thursday's June labour force data, which is expected to show the labour market remains weak.
Adding to the weak jobs outlook, the ANZ Bank said its job advertisement series fell 2.9 percent in July, and now suggests jobs growth of just 13,000 per month over the next few months.
"Growth in the demand for labour appears to have eased off slightly over the past few months," ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said when releasing the job series data.

Until Thursday, however, the U.S. market is expected to remain the guiding force on local bonds. While bonds followed the U.S. lower after Friday's strong data, they are expected to outperform Treasuries in a bearish market given positive debt market fundamentals of low inflation and still subdued growth.

Bonds outperform against Treasuries but remain mixed to other debt. NZ market firm ahead of what are expected to be weak June quarter labour data on Tuesday. Yield curve reverses flattening trend of late last week.
